mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent risk aversion from higher real rates compressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar high-rate regimes, or FEDFUNDS drops below 5.25% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs signals labor market strength, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investor confidence improves.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 50,000 by more than 10,000 jobs in a month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 30-day average (t-test p > 0.05), or employment growth reverts below 40,000 for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 120 (index) for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it indicates robust manufacturing momentum and consumer demand.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of similar INDPRO spikes, or manufacturing momentum dissipates (INDPRO falls below 115 within 30 days).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter monetary policy and reduced corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of similar inflation spikes, or CPIAUCSL reverts to below 2.5% within 45 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0% for 10 consecutive months indicates a labor market tightening that precedes a positive S&P 60-day forward return as market pricing in future growth.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a control window (p > 0.10), or UNRATE reverts to ≥4.5% within 15 days.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies; this sketch is omitted because required proxies are unavailable) would predict a positive 20-day forward return. Instead, we proxy with a combined signal: HOUST (industrial output) and GDPC1 (goods orders) both rising for two months, suggesting robust demand. This interaction effect drives the signal.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 2000 and GDPC1 > 11000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significant after controlling for lagged SPX returns (F-test p > 0.05), or both proxies revert to flat or declining for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) below 120,000 for two consecutive months in a regime of rising unemployment suggests recessionary pressure and is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 120,000 for two consecutive months and UNRATE > 5.0 for one month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of similar payrolls declines, or unemployment falls below 4.5% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) move in opposite directions for two consecutive months (INDPRO up while CPIAUCSL falls), it suggests supply-side dislocation and a negative S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases while CPIAUCSL decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of such divergent INDPRO-CPIAUCSL events, or the divergence reverses within 45 days.
